_meta: local_hard_v1 CANDIDATE roster v2 (NOT FROZEN -- founder curation pending). The humanoid-ladder instrument (rungs R1-R2, single-body servo-interface parts; founder directive 2026-07-22). Servo = MG996R, BOUGHT part, dims cited from src/forge_mind/assembly/servo.py. v2 folds the idiom survey (docs/research/2026-07-22-humanoid-bracket-idioms.md): cable_chain_link CUT (gantry idiom, domain uses molded wire grooves -- grooves now ride shin_link + torso_side_frame); battery_cradle swapped to torso_back_cover (same snap class, domain-real); waist_bracket + idler_bushing ADDED (survey's missing classes); high-load joints (shoulder/hip yokes, U-bracket) min_wall 3.0 per the survey's triangulated 2-4mm band. VERIFICATION PENDING (do not freeze without resolving): servo.py's horn BC 17.0 is provisional and BOTH research agents converged on ~14mm domain norms -- verify against a physical MG996R round horn / primary drawing; body 40.7x19.7x42.9 same tier. Briefs regenerate from servo.py constants, so a registry correction re-authors the corpus in one command. Comparator-bridge anchors ride along at freeze time by label from legacy corpora: exhaust_manifold_4to1, fan_duct, tslot_nut, desk_grommet. Rungs R3+ (subassemblies w/ mapped servos; STS3215 ingest PARTIAL -- no-flange dual-horn architecture needs its own frame contract, docs/research/2026-07-22-sts3215-facts.md) need the assembly-lane bench harness -- separate iteration.

label: servo_side_bracket
prompt: An L-shaped side-mount bracket for an MG996R hobby servo: the vertical face takes the servo's four flange screws, the base bolts to a frame with M3 screws, and the servo wire exits through a slot. MG996R interface dims are the registry-cited values (TowerPro datasheet, provisional; src/forge_mind/assembly/servo.py): tab holes 4x d4.5 on a 49.5 x 10.0 mm rectangle, horn screws 4x d2.2 on a 17.0 mm bolt circle, hub center bore d8.1.

brief.summary: L-bracket: vertical servo face with the 4-hole tab pattern and a wire slot, horizontal base with M3 mounting holes.
brief.visual_description: A sturdy L of two rectangular plates meeting at 90 degrees with a filleted root. The tall face shows four small screw holes in a wide flat rectangle pattern and one open-ended vertical slot; the flat base shows four corner holes. Uniform wall, no taper.
brief.overall_envelope_mm: 60 x 30 x 52 -- the vertical face must span the 54.4 mm servo flange; the base is deep enough for stable M3 mounting.

features.name: vertical_servo_face
features.purpose: carries the servo flange

features.name: servo_tab_holes
features.purpose: clearance for the four flange screws on the cited rectangle

features.name: wire_exit_slot
features.purpose: open-ended slot so the servo lead passes without pinching

features.name: horizontal_base
features.purpose: bolts the bracket to a frame

features.name: base_mount_holes
features.purpose: M3 clearance to the frame

features.name: root_fillet_rib
features.purpose: stiffens the 90-degree joint against servo torque

brief.print_orientation_note: Base flat on the bed; the vertical face prints upward without support (the wire slot opens upward).

label: servo_horn_hub
prompt: A round hub adapter that screws onto an MG996R round servo horn and presents a square key boss for a link. MG996R interface dims are the registry-cited values (TowerPro datasheet, provisional; src/forge_mind/assembly/servo.py): tab holes 4x d4.5 on a 49.5 x 10.0 mm rectangle, horn screws 4x d2.2 on a 17.0 mm bolt circle, hub center bore d8.1.

brief.summary: Disc that mates the round horn (center bore + 4 horn screws on the cited bolt circle) and carries a square drive boss on top.
brief.visual_description: A thick coin-like disc; from the top a small square boss rises from the center. Top view shows one center bore and four tiny screw holes evenly spaced on a circle around it. Edges lightly chamfered, everything concentric.
brief.overall_envelope_mm: 26 x 26 x 12 -- disc slightly wider than the 21 mm horn; boss height gives the link a full key.

features.name: hub_disc
features.purpose: the body that seats on the horn face

features.name: center_bore
features.purpose: clears the horn's center screw boss

features.name: horn_screw_holes
features.purpose: the four horn screws on the cited bolt circle

features.name: square_key_boss
features.purpose: keys the driven link so it cannot spin

brief.print_orientation_note: Disc face down; the boss prints upward, bores are vertical.

label: servo_c_bracket

MG996R interface dims are the registry-cited values (TowerPro datasheet, provisional; src/forge_mind/assembly/servo.py): tab holes 4x d4.5 on a 49.5 x 10.0 mm rectangle, horn screws 4x d2.2 on a 17.0 mm bolt circle, hub center bore d8.1. The servo case is 40.7 x 19.7 x 42.9 mm.

brief.summary: U-channel cradle: bottom plate with the 4 tab holes, two side walls hugging the servo case with clearance.
brief.visual_description: A squat open-topped channel like a wide staple. Flat bottom plate with four screw holes near its ends; two parallel upright walls with a rectangular window between them where the servo body sits. Slightly rounded outer corners.
brief.overall_envelope_mm: 58 x 26 x 22 -- the plate spans the 54.4 mm flange; walls stop below the flange underside.

features.purpose: takes the four flange screws from below

features.name: servo_tab_holes

features.name: side_walls
features.purpose: cradle the 19.7 mm wide case with 0.3 mm clearance per side

brief.object_name: humanoid foot plate with ankle servo mount

label: servo_u_bracket
prompt: The classic hobby-servo U-bracket for an MG996R: one arm bolts to the round horn, the opposite arm carries an idler pivot bore coaxial with the horn axis. MG996R interface dims are the registry-cited values (TowerPro datasheet, provisional; src/forge_mind/assembly/servo.py): tab holes 4x d4.5 on a 49.5 x 10.0 mm rectangle, horn screws 4x d2.2 on a 17.0 mm bolt circle, hub center bore d8.1.

brief.summary: U-shaped yoke: horn-interface arm (center bore + cited bolt circle), opposite idler arm with a coaxial pivot bore, joined by a base web.
brief.visual_description: A squared U like a tuning fork from the side. One upright arm shows the center bore ringed by four tiny holes; the facing arm shows a single larger bore exactly opposite. The connecting base is a flat web with lightly filleted inner corners. Arms parallel, bores coaxial.
brief.overall_envelope_mm: 50 x 32 x 58 -- inner span clears the 42.9 mm case height plus horn stack; arms deep enough for full bolt circles.
